criteria: With `expand` enabled, an array-valued property inside a composite token (e.g. `strokeStyle.dashArray`, `color.components`, `transition.timingFunction`) produces one expanded token per array item, instead of a single token holding the whole array.
With `expand` enabled, a token whose own value is an array (e.g. a `cubicBezier` token) produces one expanded token per array item.

Each expanded item token holds exactly one array element as its scalar value, and its key ends with the 1-based item index (e.g. `{stroke.dashArray.1}`, `{stroke.dashArray.2}`), consistent with the indexing already applied to multi-value shadow tokens.
Each expanded item token's type is the type mapped for that property (e.g. `dashArray` items are `dimension`), not the array or composite type, so per-item transforms apply to it.
Expansion of object-value tokens and multi-value (array-of-objects) shadow tokens produces the same output as before.
With `expand` disabled (the default), array values are left untouched.
The `expand` config controls — `include`/`exclude`, `typesMap`, and global vs platform-level configuration — apply to array-item expansion exactly as they do to composite expansion today.
description:
The `expand` feature only itemizes arrays whose items are objects — i.e. multi-value `shadow` tokens. Every other array value is left intact as a single expanded token holding the whole array. This affects array-valued properties inside composite tokens (e.g. `strokeStyle.dashArray`, `color.components`, `transition.timingFunction`) and token types whose own value is an array (e.g. `cubicBezier`).

Example: with `expand` enabled, a `strokeStyle` token with `dashArray: ['0.5rem', '0.25rem']` currently produces one `dashArray` token whose value is the array. Expected: it produces one token per array item (`dashArray.1` = `'0.5rem'`, `dashArray.2` = `'0.25rem'`), matching how a two-shadow token already becomes `1`/`2` groups.

Root cause: expansion is only triggered when the token value is a plain object or an array in which every item is a plain object (the multi-shadow case). Once expanding, only plain-object property values are recursed into; any other property value is stored verbatim, so arrays never itemize. The array-item code path also assumes items are objects (it enumerates their entries), which is why an earlier attempt to treat arrays generically produced bogus per-character tokens and was reverted to a plain-object guard. Supporting arrays of primitives requires a distinct itemization path that emits one scalar-valued token per array element.

The key is removed and nothing was ever written in its place.

Repro (expand on):

```js
tokens: { stroke: { type: 'strokeStyle', value: { dashArray: [], lineCap: 'round' } } }
```

- base (`ting-base`): `{stroke.dashArray}` preserved with `value: []`
- HEAD: keys are `["{stroke.lineCap}"]` — `{stroke.dashArray}` is **gone** from `tokenMap`, `sd.tokens`, and every platform export

`dashArray: []` is a realistic, meaningful value (SVG: empty dash array = solid stroke). The token vanishes silently from all generated output, and any consumer referencing `{stroke.dashArray}` gets a broken reference. Same drop occurs with `$value: []`, at platform-level expand, and for `dashArray: [{}]` (array whose items are all empty objects — also preserved by base, dropped at HEAD). This is a delete with no confirmation that its replacement was written.

Fix should follow the design guidance, not add a guard: the flaw is that the decomposition *predicate* (`:209`) and the decomposition *producer* (`:223-243`) disagree — a value can be judged itemizable and then yield zero items. Make expansion one step: a single value→replacement-tokens mapping whose result is swapped in for the original key only when it is an expansion; a value with no decomposable items (`[]`, `[{}]`) is not an expansion and must remain the token it already is. notes:
Array itemization is opt-in: it only happens when `expand` is enabled for the token, so users with `expand: true` and array-valued tokens such as DTCG `fontFamily` (a string array) will also see those itemized; `include`/`exclude`/`typesMap` are the documented way to scope this, and the behavior change should be called out in the changelog.

Consistency constraint: the existing multi-value convention only adds an index when the array has more than one item (`arr.length > 1`); decide and apply the single-item case consistently rather than inventing a second convention.

Out of scope: arrays of objects nested as a *property value* (e.g. a multi-shadow embedded inside a border) — the issue covers primitive arrays (`dashArray`, `components`, `cubicBezier`).

Type-mapping gotchas: `color.components` has no entry in the built-in DTCG types map, so its items would get an unmapped type unless the map is extended (e.g. `components` -> `number`); the token type for items of a top-level array token such as `cubicBezier` also needs a sensible scalar mapping. Note the built-in map currently maps `strokeStyle.dashArray` to `dimension`, while the docs' DTCG types map example still shows `other` — reconcile the docs as part of this work.

Guard against regression: string values must never be itemized per character (the reason the plain-object guard was introduced), and platform-level expansion must keep adjusting the `path` metadata of the newly created item tokens.
snapshot_summary: The agent refactored `lib/utils/expandObjectTokens.js` so that array-valued tokens and composite properties (e.g. `strokeStyle.dashArray`, `color.components`, `cubicBezier`) expand into one indexed scalar token per array item (e.g. `{stroke.dashArray.1}`) instead of a single token holding the whole array, extracting new private helpers `expandTokenValue`, `buildExpandedToken`, and `expandProp`; it updated `__tests__/utils/expandObjectTokens.test.js` expectations accordingly and added `.changeset/expand-array-values.md` (bumped `minor`). Concerns: the exported `expandTokenInMap` was renamed to a non-exported `expandTokenValue`, a public API removal that may warrant a major bump and that the changeset doesn't mention; verification was done via ad hoc `/tmp/v_*.mjs` scripts that were deleted rather than committed tests; and the diff was truncated, so the full recursion/`shouldExpand` behavior and whether arrays survive when `expand` is disabled couldn't be confirmed here.
